internal_alignment: Decoding RF.1.3(a), (b): know the spelling-sound correspondences for common consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh, ph as one sound each); decode regularly spelled one-syllable words. RF.1.1(a) as a light touch on Page 5 only (capital at the start, period at the end). Printed words throughout: the child reads letters and words, never blends by ear without print (that was Resource 1, Sounds in Words). All child-reading words are one-syllable, short vowels only, plus known blends. No long vowels, final-e, or vowel teams (Resource 3); no two-syllable words (Resource 10). Internal record only; no standards codes appear on any child page, and no separate answer key is published for this pack.
pack: Grade 1 Reading: Word Detectives: Consonant Digraphs

pages_detail.activities: Adult models each digraph sound first, then reads the example word aloud. The child circles the two letters in each word that make one sound.
pages_detail.title: Meet the Digraphs

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the word and draws a line to the matching picture. Pictures are in mixed order; no picture sits beside its own word.
pages_detail.title: Read and Match: Digraphs at the Start

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the word, then circles the two letters at the end that make one sound. The picture beside each word checks the meaning.
pages_detail.title: Find the Sound at the End

pages_detail.activities: Child reads each word in the bank and writes it in the column of its digraph. Phil is a person's name, so it starts with a capital P. No other untaught vowel pattern is introduced.
pages_detail.title: Sort the Words

pages_detail.activities: Child reads the sentence and draws a line to the picture it tells about. Every word is decodable from taught patterns or a high-frequency word. The adult points out the capital at the start and the period at the end.
answers: The fish is in the dish. (fish in a shallow dish)
The chick can sit on the bench. (chick on a bench)
The ship is on the sand. (ship on sand)
The chick is in the shop. (chick inside a shop)
pages_detail.title: Read the Sentences
